clue.text: Shriek from engineers caught in swindle

indicators.note: the engineers are held inside the swindle, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a scam is a swindle
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone cries out on discovering engineers involved in a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud piercing cry, the same as a shriek.

clue.text: Wholly vindicate

definitions.meaning: to free from blame or suspicion

explanation.surface: A plea for complete exoneration.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means completely (got clean away), and as a verb it means to declare someone innocent.

clue.text: Unauthorised rush to join union

parts.note: reads like workers stampeding into a trade union without permission, but means running off in secret to marry

explanation.surface: Workers make an unofficial dash to sign up with a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away secretly to get married is an unsanctioned dash into matrimony, the union of marriage.

clue.text: It is really crazy to free capital

parts.note: mad means really crazy
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Someone declares it insane to liberate the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish city is the capital of Spain.

clue.text: Amazing chap hiding in Kent

parts.note: super means amazing or excellent
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A remarkable fellow lies low somewhere in the English county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent here is not the county but Clark Kent, the mild reporter whose identity the comic-book hero hides behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-strip hero conceals himself in the guise of the reporter Clark Kent.

clue.text: Cannot decide whether it has been ruined deliberately?

definitions.text: Cannot decide whether it has been ruined deliberately?

parts.words: Cannot decide whether it has been ruined deliberately?
parts.note: the second half reads the idiom literally: damaged by deliberate selection rather than by accident

explanation.surface: Someone puzzles over whether a thing was wrecked on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes having so many options that deciding is hard; read literally it means wrecked by intent.

clue.text: It's safe to criticise one who never grows up

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone says it is harmless to find fault with an eternal child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a strongbox, called a PETER in thieves' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's character is the boy who refuses to grow older.

clue.text: Genuine mark made by kingdom

parts.note: real means genuine
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An authentic stamp left by a monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain ruled by a monarch, that is a kingdom.

clue.text: At sea, stop trouble from rats

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up or disturb, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor at sea fends off a nuisance from rodents aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rats' are not rodents but deserters, people who abandon their side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats in the slang sense are turncoats, people who abandon a cause or faith.

clue.text: Call to resume fight: unconscious after less than a minute

indicators.note: unconscious comes after the time phrase, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: seconds are units shorter than a minute
out means knocked unconscious

explanation.surface: A boxer is knocked cold almost instantly as the bell sounds again.
explanation.definitionFit: The referee's cry clears the corner helpers from the ring before the next boxing round.

clue.text: Hello, sailor!

parts.note: reads as a cheeky greeting to a seaman, but is the greeting a seaman uses himself

explanation.surface: A flirtatious hail to a passing seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: This nautical cry is the traditional way to hail another ship.

clue.text: Spontaneity of solicitor's generous offer?

definitions.meaning: acting voluntarily, of one's own accord
a lawyer offering to draw up a testament at no cost

explanation.surface: A lawyer's unprompted offer of free legal help.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without compulsion is spontaneity; jokingly, a no-charge testament drafted by a lawyer is a gift.

clue.text: Distant meteor crashed

indicators.note: something crashed is smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A space rock came down far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means far off, a synonym of distant.

clue.text: Talented contribution to tableau

indicators.note: the letters make up part of the word that follows, contributing to it

explanation.surface: Praise for a gifted performer's part in a staged scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or capable, a synonym of talented.

clue.text: Weapon dispersed Orange mob

indicators.note: a dispersed crowd is scattered, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Arms are used to break up a crowd of Orangemen marching in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orange mob suggests Northern Ireland's Protestant Orange Order marchers.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved throwing stick of Australian Aborigines is a hunting weapon.

clue.text: Boring partner who lives with you?

parts.note: flat means dull or boring
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A dull companion who shares your home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharing a rented apartment with you is that person's housemate.

clue.text: Rival deal that is in splinters

parts.note: a match is an equal or rival
deal is a kind of pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A competing contract falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like an agreement but is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood smashed into tiny fragments is said to be reduced to splinters.

clue.text: What does cashmere come from? I really have no idea!

indicators.note: asks what this word is a rearrangement of, signalling a reverse anagram

explanation.surface: Someone asked about the origin of a soft wool shrugs helplessly.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the letters of the answer, rearranged, give 'cashmere'. 'What does' frames the question.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase is a way to say you do not know.

clue.text: Last product, probably not a single one sold

definitions.text: Last product, probably not a single one sold

parts.words: Last product, probably not a single one sold
parts.note: a last is a cobbler's foot-shaped form; shoes come off it and are sold in pairs, not singly

explanation.surface: A final product that failed to find a single buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes and boots are made on a last and normally sold as a pair.

clue.text: Decide what to do with a little money

definitions.meaning: to settle a matter by flipping a coin

definitions.text: what to do with a little money
definitions.meaning: flipping a small coin into the air

explanation.surface: Someone ponders how to spend some small change.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin is a way to settle a choice, and it is also simply what one does with a coin.

clue.text: Competitor takes quiet course

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a course of bricks is a layer

explanation.surface: A competitor follows a calm route.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a participant in a game or sport, a competitor.

clue.text: We hear bloke is one that spouts regularly

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: Gossip that some man talks constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the hot spring's name is pronounced to rhyme with 'freezer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spring erupts water at intervals, like Old Faithful.

clue.text: Vow to profane

definitions.meaning: to use irreverent or obscene language

explanation.surface: Someone promises to commit sacrilege.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both to promise solemnly and to use blasphemous or obscene language.

clue.text: Halo over this port?

parts.note: a halo sits above a saint's sacred crown, giving the name of a Welsh ferry town

explanation.surface: A glowing ring hangs above a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh ferry port on Anglesey sails to Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglesey harbour town is a port; read in two parts it names what a halo crowns.

clue.text: A teetotaller in charge of lofty area

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal
IC means in charge

explanation.surface: A non-drinker runs a high-up place.
explanation.definitionFit: The room right under the roof is a high space in a house.

clue.text: Parting gesture from one on the sea

definitions.meaning: a hand movement used in farewell
a swell or breaker on the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone waves goodbye from a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a hand signal of farewell and a ridge of water travelling on the ocean.

clue.text: Stuck up a couple of rhymes

explanation.surface: Two verses pinned on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means haughty or snooty, and its two halves rhyme with each other.

clue.text: With wild rage, give distress

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fury is turned into misery for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to wrong or upset someone, causing distress.

clue.text: Make smaller and subdue

definitions.meaning: to conquer, as in reducing a fortress

explanation.surface: A plea to shrink and conquer.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both to lessen in size and, in an older sense, to bring under control.
